transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Jordan Meyer (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (CTO, HearthLabs), Maya Lin (Platform Eng), Ethan Cho (Security Lead), Nina Patel (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood presented preliminary shadow benchmarking results, discussed access gaps (VPC peering, gateway rules), agreed to run a larger latency bench with 8k context and collect full traces. Security questions around KMS and audit logs remain open. Next steps: bench CSV, VPC creds, SE deep-dive scheduled.

Topics:
- Shadow benchmark results (latency distribution, p95/p99)
- Access gating: staging VPC, port rules, jumpbox
- Security: KMS, data residency, audit logs
- Tuning: KV cache warmup, batching, quant profiles
- Rollout considerations: canary vs immediate traffic shift

Action-items (captured above): see action_items field

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Jordan: "Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick check, am I audible?"
[00:06] Carlos: "Yep, loud and clear. We got a few folks on our side, just FYI Maya will drop off around 15:30 for another stand-up."
[00:12] Jordan: "Great. Priya, you wanna kick off the bench readout?"
[00:15] Priya: "Sure. So we ran two shadow runs against your staging traffic, one with default quant profile and one with the aggressive 4-bit quantization. The main takeaways: median token latency was ~42ms, p95 around 180ms, p99 spiked near 620ms on the larger sequences. There was a consistent tail when KV cache cold starts happened — so the first 6-8 requests post cache invalidation had higher cost. The CSV and charts are in the link I posted — bit.ly/redwood-shadow-aug21 (note: link is short reference in chat)."
[00:52] Nina: "Can you repeat the p99? I think you said 620 but our local traces show closer to 480 for the same payload earlier."
[01:01] Priya: "Yeah, so on run B we saw 480 median p99, but on run A with heavier burst traffic we had a 620ms tail. There might be a correlation with sequence length and batch packing. Also, uh, one of the traces shows a retry from the gateway which bumped latency up — that was a client-side 502 retry that, like, doubled the observed p99. We tried to filter but not everything got cleaned in the auto-agg."
[01:30] Maya: "Is that the gateway retry from our side or from Redwood's side? We need to pinpoint ownership for the spike."
[01:36] Priya: "Good question. Most of the gateway retries in those traces are 504 timeouts on your side LB, but there's also a small set that looks like transient infra throttling on the serving host during warmup. We flagged them in the spreadsheet — column F, 'retry_source' — but the transcript auto-extract munged some headers so sorry if it's messy."
[02:02] Ethan: "From security: were the traces scrubbed? We can't have PII in the shared CSVs."
[02:06] Jordan: "Yes, Priya anonymized payloads, only timing, token counts and trace ids — no user texts. We'll still send a sanitized version tech-only."
[02:15] Priya: "Right, sanitized. But Ethan, quick note: if you want full traces we'll need an NDA supplement; otherwise we provide the aggregated and redacted CSVs which should be enough for tuning."
[02:29] Ethan: "Understood. We'll review and let you know if we need the deeper traces and start the legal loop if necessary."
[02:35] Carlos: "On the access side, we still have a hang for the staging jumpbox. Maya, can you confirm the port access?"
[02:40] Maya: "We opened 443 and 5200 to Redwood's egress IPs, but I think there's a mismatch — Priya your IP list had two addresses, we only allowed one. I'm gonna share the firewall rule in the chat now."
[02:54] Priya: "Ah right — sorry I forgot to include the HA secondary. I'm pasting the updated netblock in chat: 34.87.112.0/28 and 34.87.113.0/28."
[03:05] Maya: "Got it — will add second block and then we'll smoke test the peering."
[03:10] Jordan: "Excellent. Quick question to the group: are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the initial pilot? We provided both cost delta slides last week."
[03:18] Carlos: "For now hosted looks easier, but we need to validate tail latency. If tail is unacceptable we might go dedicated. The dedicated cost hit is something we'll need to present to finance — Jordan, can you give a ballpark monthly number for the dedicated slice to support 200 rps sustained and 2k burst?"
[03:34] Jordan: "Yes, I'll send a concise pricing matrix after the call — dedicated monthly range plus per-token variance for quantization. Putting that as an action. But keep in mind, the routing fallback means we could start hosted and failover to dedicated for peak windows."
[03:50] Nina: "On tuning: what are the immediate knobs? KV cache warmup? Batch sizing? Quantization?"
[03:56] Priya: "All of the above. For this workload our recommended quick wins are: 1) prefix caching for repeated contexts (you have a lot of system prompts so warmup helps), 2) slightly larger minibatches during low-concurrency windows to reduce per-token cost without harming p95, and 3) try the conservative 5-bit quant first — the 4-bit showed some increase in tail variance on long sequences. We'll run a 1k-sample bench with 8k context to confirm."
[04:30] Maya: "Is prefix caching configurable in Redwood Private? We have constraints around data retention and want to ensure ephemeral cache only lives in GPU memory, not written to disk."
[04:39] Priya: "Yes, cache is memory-only by default. In Private we can disable persistent snapshotting. We also support prefix-only caching policies that drop after X minutes. We'll document settings."
[04:50] Ethan: "KMS question: for Private we prefer using our KMS — can Redwood integrate with our HSM keys and support enveloping?"
[04:58] Jordan: "Short answer: yes. Longer answer: we support customer KMS via external key management, and for on-prem we can plug into your HSM with an audited connector. We'll send the KMS integration architecture diagram — that's a doc Priya will attach."
[05:14] Priya: "I'll add KMS diagram and the step-by-step for initial key provisioning to the share. Also note that the audit logs include token-level metadata (no payload) if you enable that; you can set retention at the project level."
[05:26] Carlos: "Residency — if we keep data in EU for some customers, is there control on model routing?"
[05:32] Jordan: "Yes, you can pin region and have routing policies. For private you control region. Hosted supports region pinning for enterprise tenants. We'll share the routing policy doc."
[05:40] Maya: "Back to bench specifics: the bench you ran used our real traffic replay or synthetic?"
[05:45] Priya: "Traffic replay from your anonymized staging logs — we did not replay production. The sequence length histogram was taken from your last 24h staging snapshot. One caveat: the replay tool preserves inter-arrival timing but we had to compress windows to finish within our maintenance window so burst patterns might be more aggressive than your steady-state."
[06:06] Nina: "That may explain the p99 spikes then."
[06:08] Priya: "Exactly. Also we noticed a small number of very long system messages that dominated sample size; we can trim those for a second pass to see baseline behavior."
[06:20] Jordan: "Ok, let's talk fallback playbook briefly. If we see p99 above 1s in production, what's the quick mitigation? Priya?"
[06:26] Priya: "You can set a policy to route 10-20% traffic to a cheaper lower-latency model or lower context window (reduce max_tokens), and have automatic rollback. Also enable aggressive prefix caching for that route. If it's infra, dedicated capacity can be hot-swapped but that takes time, so we prefer routing policies as a first approach."
[06:46] Ethan: "How do those policies surface in the console? We need RBAC to restrict who can change them."
[06:51] Jordan: "Console has per-route RBAC and audit trails; only admins can change routing policies by default. We'll send a screenshot and the exact RBAC roles."
[06:59] Carlos: "About the bench CSV — can Priya highlight which rows we should focus on to make a call between hosted vs dedicated?"
[07:06] Priya: "Focus on p95/p99, retry counts, and 'kv_cold_count' column. Also look at 'seq_len' and 'batch_size' columns to understand whether tail is sequence-driven. I'll annotate the CSV and add a summary tab with recommended action."
[07:20] Maya: "Cool. Any red flags from infra on your side?"
[07:23] Priya: "We saw one instance where our scheduler evicted a pod during a maintenance batch — that was a config on our test cluster not in prod; flagged it but not a systemic issue. Also a couple of timeouts traced to your LB config needed longer idle timeouts for streaming responses."
[07:40] Maya: "We can increase idle timeout to 120s; it's currently 60s."
[07:44] Carlos: "Do we have an exact list of network requirements? Our security team wants a minimal allowed egress list."
[07:50] Jordan: "Yes: we'll send an egress allowlist, plus IP ranges for dedicated endpoints. Priya will paste the specific /28s in chat now."
[07:57] Priya: "Pasted. Also note we prefer VPC peering but can support guarded public endpoints if peering is delayed."
[08:05] Ethan: "If we do VPC peering, what's the observability surface? We need to capture request tracing tied to our trace ids."
[08:12] Priya: "We can propagate your trace IDs through the X-Request-Id header and include them in our traces. The logs we send will map to your ids. Full distributed tracing requires setting up our tracer endpoint or shipping spans to your collector; we can do either."
[08:26] Ethan: "Okay we'll plan to ship spans to our collector during the SE deep-dive."
[08:31] Jordan: "Great — quick time check, we're 8 minutes in? Sorry, 8 minutes left on our scheduled blocker but we have time, let's keep going."
[08:40] Nina: "One more thing about quality: do you have regression monitoring tied to our evals? We want to tie perf regressions to prompt testsets."
[08:48] Priya: "Yes, Redwood Optimize can run prompt-level baselines and alert on drift. It can also tie quality deltas to specific model/quant changes. We'll enable a baseline for your key prompt sets once you give us the testset."
[09:02] Carlos: "We'll share a small gold set — maybe 50 prompts. We'll also want to test hallucination rates on critical intents."
[09:08] Jordan: "Perfect. So to recap preliminary items: Priya runs expanded bench, Redwood shares price matrix and egress list, HearthLabs adds second netblock and shares jumpbox creds, Security reviews KMS integration. Any other blockers?"
[09:20] Maya: "We still need the SSO flow tested for access to the console. Is that in scope this week?"
[09:26] Jordan: "SSO is on our integration plan. We can do an SSO smoke next week; we'll need your SAML metadata. I'll add that to next steps."
[09:33] Ethan: "Also, audit log retention policies — default is 90 days?"
[09:38] Priya: "Default enterprise retention is 90 days, we can extend for a fee or you can export logs to your storage. We'll document options."
[09:46] Carlos: "Sounds good. One final ask: can you outline the timeline to go from pilot to canary and then to full roll — ballpark weeks?"
[09:54] Jordan: "Typical is 2 weeks pilot (staging+shadow), 1 week canary ramp, then 2-4 weeks full roll depending on risk. With a dedicated contract that can accelerate some infra steps. I'll put a timeline in the follow-up note."
[10:08] Priya: "I'll schedule a 60-minute SE deep-dive for augmenting KV cache warmup strategies and quant profiles — proposing 2026-08-27 at 10am PT. Does that work?"
[10:18] Carlos: "Works for me. Maya?"
[10:20] Maya: "Yep."
[10:21] Ethan: "Good for security too."
[10:23] Jordan: "Okay great. Anything else from HearthLabs?"
[10:26] Nina: "No, just please be explicit in the CSV about which rows map to which sample id, we had trouble correlating earlier."
[10:33] Priya: "Will do — I'll add an 'owner_map' tab mapping sample ids to run configs. Also I'm going to sanitize the sheet further so the headers align with your naming conventions."
[10:44] Jordan: "Alright folks, thanks. We'll share the bench artifacts and the pricing matrix today. Let's reconvene post-bench next Monday as a quick 30m check. I'll send calendar invites. Thanks all."
[10:57] Carlos: "Thanks everyone."
[11:00] (call ends)

Notes about transcript: automated speaker labels sometimes incorrect; some technical terms got mangled (e.g., 'K-V cache' vs 'KV cache', 'Redwood Optimize' spelled 'Redwood Optimise' in caption). Refer to artifacts linked in chat for canonical names.
